body:
Are you using transactions when you save your records? Perhaps the issue is related to the incorrect isolation level?

As for the methods that are involved in saving:
- Table::save() calls Table::_processSave() in a transaction by default.
- Table::_processSave() uses Cake\ORM\Query to build an insert/update query for the top level entity.
- After inserting, the driver's lastInsertID() method is called which uses the underlying PDO method and the entity is updated.
- AssociationCollection::saveChildren() is called for each child relation. This method calls the saveAssociated() method on each relation (HasMany in your case).
- The association classes set foreign keys and use the association target (Comments in your case) to save each associated entity.
Sounds like a transaction isolation level. I would suggest that you set it to 'serializable' for this transaction
We could use the method we use in Postgres for extra safety, but kinda sad that the PDO driver is not safe, if it is a race condition

You will need to read the documentation for SQL server on transaction isolation levels, I'm not too familiar with it so I cannot recommend the way to do it. I'm just telling you what has been a fix for me in similar situations when using MySQL.

In Postgres we use a different insert statement that immediately returns all the inserted columns back in the statement. It is a bit slower, but it is safer.

@Laykou You could implement a similar feature by updating the `_buildInsertPart` in `Cake\Database\SqlserverCompiler` to include the `OUTPUT INSERTED.*` clause in the correct place. This should let the insert query read out the inserted data.
It should probably be `Inserted.*` as you don;t know what the name of the primary key  column is
Yeah, I would get all the columns. Also if the change helps fix your issue would you be able to do a pull request?

Surely, if it helps I will do a pull-request. Only one thing is not clear to me: When I retrieve all columns how to update the ID of the entity in the PHP object? Because this `_buildInsertPart` is only for building the query. But where is it executed and manipulating with `Model\Entity`?
That will happen automatically @Laykou, or at least it should
@Laykou This is where the magic happens https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/3.0/src/Database/Statement/StatementDecorator.php#L280

Hmm I don't think it is working for me.

The `$table -> save()` method is returning `false` with the `OUTPUT Inserted.id` but without it, everything is OK. I tried to debug it, but I am kind of lost in the core code :)

As I know the `$statement -> rowCount()` in https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/3.0/src/ORM/Table.php#L1326 is returning `-1` so that mean's to me that the `ÌNSERT` statement doesn't return the number of affected records anymore or what. But when I tried to run the query manually, it behaves like `SELECT` - returns inserted row. So it is working.
That's odd, I wouldn't have expected -1 rows. That might be an issue with pdo_sqlsrv, but should be something we can work around.

I can confirm it is an issue with pdo_sqlsrv. I am really looking forward for a work around, but I am not able to do it, since I don't fully understand how the core works and what changes I can make.

I tried it with PHP 5.4 with windows pdo extension, and PHP 5.6 with unofficial windows pdo extension. Both returned `-1` and the `INSERT` didn't inserted any rows. However I noticed that the primary key incremented. So when I later tried to INSERT other rows normally (for example through direct SQL command), some primary key values were skipped.

Also when I tried `var_dump( $statement ->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) )` in `Cake\ORM\Table@_insert` method, it returned all data as expected (here I noticed the increasing primary key).  But as I said, data were not stored in database.

I'm not sure if this helps, but this is all I know about this issue.

I was also looking at other MSSQL commands like `SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY()` but all of them were marked as not consistent and everyone refers to `OUTPUT Inserted.*`, so this is a correct solution.
If pdo_sqlsrv is failing to handle `INSERT...OUTPUT` correctly we have our hands tied a bit.

Yeah I know. But according to this http://pt2.php.net/manual/en/pdo.lastinsertid.php#105580 it should work, so I don't know, what could possibly go wrong. I will try this example by itself an see if it still works.
